title: Cammack to host veterans town hall in Ocala with Congressman Luttrell on July 10
text:
Cammack to host veterans town hall in Ocala with Congressman Luttrell on July 10
Congresswoman Kat Cammack will host a Veterans Town Hall on July 10 at the College of Central Florida in Ocala, joined by Congressman Morgan Luttrell. The event will feature a fireside conversation between the two representatives about issues facing veterans, followed by an audience question-and-answer session.
The program is scheduled to begin with a presentation of the Colors, a reading of "Old Glory," the Pledge of Allegiance, and recognition of local veterans. Cammack said, "We're lucky to represent so many incredible veterans in this district, and they deserve real answers about the issues they're facing. Morgan is coming to Ocala to talk about the work he's leading on the Veterans' Affairs Committee, and to hear directly from our veterans. I want every one of them in that room Friday night."
The event will take place at the Harvey R. Klein Conference Center at 3001 SW College Road (SR 200 campus). Doors open at 5:15 PM and the program runs from 6:00 PM to 7:05 PM. Seating is limited to 350 attendees and available on a first-come, first-served basis; veterans will be admitted and seated first. Walk-ins are welcome as space allows.
Attendees are encouraged to arrive early with their Eventbrite confirmation for check-in; free parking is available on campus. Questions for the Q&A session should be submitted by card during check-in and will be answered as time permits. Outside food or drinks are not permitted, but bottled water will be provided.
The venue is accessible and service animals are welcome; those needing accommodations such as ADA seating or ASL interpretation should contact Cammack's Ocala district office ahead of time. Members of the media planning to attend should contact Rafael Struve via email; press coverage is allowed.
Kat Cammack has served in Congress representing Florida’s 3rd District since 2021 after replacing Ted Yoho, according to her official website. She was born in Denver in 1988, lives in Gainesville, previously served in the Florida House of Representatives, and graduated from Metropolitan State University of Denver with a BA.
